market_question: Will Ethereum dip to $1,500 by December 31, 2026?
reasoning: Ethereum has not traded below $1,500 since early 2023 and is currently near $3,400. A drop to $1,500 would require a >55% decline from current levels, which would be an extreme tail event even for crypto. Institutional support via ETFs, staking demand, and ongoing network upgrades make a sustained move that low unlikely within 13 months. While a brief wick to $1,500 on a 1-minute candle is possible during a flash crash, such dislocations are rare, giving a true probability much lower than the market's 44%.
evidence_points: ETH last traded below $1,500 in November 2022 (post-FTX) and has not revisited that level since.
Current ETH price (~$3,400) implies a >55% decline needed to hit $1,500 — a magnitude comparable to the 2018 and 2022 bear markets but with stronger fundamentals today.
The condition only requires a 1-minute candle wick, but even flash crashes rarely penetrate such deep historical support levels without a systemic shock.
sources_consulted: Ethereum ETF flows and institutional adoption data
